candidates.sql:
SELECT MAX(T2.`Percent (%) Eligible Free (Ages 5-17)`) AS HighestEligibleFreeRate
FROM satscores AS T1
INNER JOIN frpm AS T2 ON T1.cds = T2.CDSCode
WHERE CAST(T1.NumGE1500 AS REAL) / T1.NumTstTakr > 0.3;

SELECT MAX(`Free Meal Count (Ages 5-17)` * 1.0 / `Enrollment (Ages 5-17)`) AS highest_eligible_free_rate
FROM frpm
JOIN satscores ON frpm.CDSCode = satscores.cds
WHERE satscores.NumTstTakr > 0
  AND satscores.NumGE1500 * 1.0 / satscores.NumTstTakr > 0.3
  AND `Enrollment (Ages 5-17)` > 0

SELECT 
    T2.account_id,
    (SELECT MAX(A11) - MIN(A11) FROM district) AS salary_gap
FROM 
    client AS T1
INNER JOIN 
    account AS T2 ON T1.district_id = T2.district_id
INNER JOIN 
    district AS T3 ON T1.district_id = T3.district_id
WHERE 
    T1.gender = 'F'
ORDER BY

FROM client

JOIN account ON disp.account_id = account.account_id
WHERE client.gender = 'F'
  AND client.birth_date = (SELECT MIN(birth_date) FROM client WHERE gender = 'F')

While a permanent is phased out, it’s treated as though it doesn’t exist. It can’t be the target of spells or abilities, its static abilities have no effect on the game, its triggered abilities can’t trigger, it can’t attack or block, and so on.
Phasing out doesn’t cause any “leaves the battlefield” abilities to trigger. Similarly, phasing in won’t cause any “enters the battlefield” abilities to trigger.
Any one-shot effects that are waiting “until [this] leaves the battlefield,” such as that of Kitesail Freebooter, won’t happen when a permanent phases out.

Any continuous effects with a “for as long as” duration such as that of Awakener Druid ignore phased-out objects. Any such effects will expire if their conditions are no longer met after ignoring the phased-out objects.

SELECT 
    CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN sets.isOnlineOnly = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100.0 / COUNT(*) AS percentage_online_only
FROM 
    sets
INNER JOIN 
    set_translations
ON 
    sets.code = set_translations.setCode
WHERE 
    set_translations.language = 'Portuguese (Brazil)';

SELECT CAST(SUM(c.isOnlineOnly = 1) AS FLOAT) / COUNT(*) * 100 AS percentage
FROM foreign_data AS f
JOIN cards AS c ON f.uuid = c.uuid
WHERE f.language = 'Portuguese (Brazil)'

LEFT JOIN legalities ON cards.uuid = legalities.uuid AND legalities.status = 'banned'
WHERE cards.artist = 'Allen Williams'

SELECT posts.Title
FROM comments

LIMIT 1;

SELECT Text
FROM comments
WHERE UserId IN (
    SELECT postHistory.UserId
    FROM postHistory
    JOIN posts ON postHistory.PostId = posts.Id
    WHERE posts.Title = 'Why square the difference instead of taking the absolute value in standard deviation?'
)

FROM 
    badges
WHERE 
    Name = 'Student';

WHERE Name = 'Student'

SELECT

    COUNT(DISTINCT T2.UserId) AS UniqueCommenters
FROM 
    postHistory AS T1

    comments AS T2 
ON

WHERE 
    T1.PostId = 3720;

SELECT PostHistoryTypeId,
       (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT UserId) FROM comments WHERE PostId = 3720) AS unique_commenters
FROM postHistory
WHERE PostId = 3720

SELECT p.Score
FROM posts p
WHERE p.Tags LIKE (

    FROM tags
    ORDER BY Count DESC
    LIMIT 1
)

FROM postLinks AS T1
INNER JOIN posts AS T2 ON T1.PostId = T2.Id
WHERE T2.AnswerCount <= 2
  AND T1.CreationDate LIKE '2010-%';

SELECT CAST(COUNT(pl.Id) AS REAL) / 12
FROM postLinks pl
JOIN posts p ON pl.PostId = p.Id
WHERE strftime('%Y', pl.CreationDate) = '2010' AND p.AnswerCount <= 2

result: Are you asking about how to reduce the effect of outliers or when to use the log of some variable?
I think that the OP is saying "I've heard of people using the log on input variables: why do they do that?"

If I am not mistaken, 

linear regression is the estimation of coefficients that define a good linear map from X to Y.

 ANOVA is a test to know if there is significant differences in X when Y take two different values.  

Can you explain us why you think they are the same?
Really great question.  The best way to understand something is from multiple direction of explanation.

Are you refering to the following paper?
Kuk, A.Y.C. (1984) All subsets regression in a proportional hazards model. Biometrika, 71, 587-592

    amount integer, -- example: [50, 200, 3000],
    source text, -- example: [Dues, Fundraising, School Appropration],
    notes text, -- example: [Secured donations to help pay for speaker gifts., Annual funding from Student Government., Ad revenue for use on flyers used to advertise ...],
    link_to_member text, -- example: [reccW7q1KkhSKZsea, recTjHY5xXhvkCdVT, recUdRhbhcEO1Hk5r],
    FOREIGN KEY (link_to_member) REFERENCES member(member_id)

    first_name text, -- example: [Angela, Grant, Luisa],
    last_name text, -- example: [Sanders, Gilmour, Guidi],
    email text, -- example: [angela.sanders@lpu.edu, grant.gilmour@lpu.edu, luisa.guidi@lpu.edu],
    position text, -- example: [Member, Inactive, President],
    t_shirt_size text, -- example: [Medium, X-Large, Large],
    phone text, -- example: [(651) 928-4507, 403-555-1310, 442-555-5882],
    zip integer, -- example: [55108, 29440, 10002],
    link_to_major text, -- example: [recxK3MHQFbR9J5uO, rec7BxKpjJ7bNph3O, recdIBgeU38UbV2sy],
